old.support_text: HBx contributes to inflammation by triggering the release of proinflammatory cytokines including IL-6, MCP-1, CXCL2, and HMGB1, and induces oxidative stress by upregulating ROS production. old.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

old.support_text: An epigenetic regimen with non-cytotoxic doses of the demethylating compound 5-azacytidine restored the anti-HBV action of IFNα in epigenetically reprogrammed HepG2-NTCP cells (REP-HepG2-NTCP). This inhibitory effect was associated with enhancement of IFNα-mediated induction of critical interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), which was limited in non-reprogrammed cells. Re-expression of 2'-5'-oligoadenylate synthetase 1 (OAS1) and interferon regulatory factor 9 (IRF9) resulted from an epigenetically driven unmasking of these genes in reprogrammed cells.
